newsitem.title: UK: Centrica terminates Beryl gas contracts.
newsitem.headline: Centrica terminates Beryl gas contracts.

text.p: Centrica plc, the supply arm of former UK gas monopoly holder British Gas, has terminated three separate natural gas contracts supplying a total of around five billion therms from the North Sea's Beryl field.
Centrica has reached agreements with Amerada Hess, Enterprise plc and OMV (UK) Ltd and the contracts will terminate on October 1 1998.
Centrica will pay compensation for the termination of the agreements, but a spokesman for the company said the figures involved were "not in the commercial domain."
The company said in a statement that the total amounted to less than a quarter of a percent of its net assets.

Centrica had previously terminated its Beryl contract with operator Mobil in December 1996. The company said that including the most recent contracts to be terminated, Centrica has now reduced its price and volume commitments on over 30 billion therms.
Beryl is around 200 miles north-east of Aberdeen. The owners sold most of their production under a long term contract to British Gas from October 1992.
